intuition.title: Study context: Alkaline selenium source
intuition.text: The authors propose selenide, selenite and polyselenide species in the deep-red stock and report stability only with OH− concentration greater than 10 M. The value describes the source explanation, not a separately measured batch concentration.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2, Equations 1–2 and selenium-source discussion

intuition.title: Study context: Cadmium complex
intuition.text: The authors attribute reduced hydroxide by-product to cadmium complexation and discuss release of Cd2+ as precipitation proceeds. The source reports no CdSeO3 detected by XRD or XPS. No separate quantified bare-cadmium control recipe or measured by-product fraction is supplied.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Equations 3–5 and mechanism discussion

intuition.title: Study context: Workup and excess reagents
intuition.text: The source says dilute 0.1 M HCl can remove small Cd(OH)2 amounts and water can remove excess cadmium complex; excess elemental Se can precipitate during washing and be difficult to remove. These are conditional source explanations, not extra measured batches.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3, Workup and stoichiometry discussion

intuition.title: Study context: Temperature scope
intuition.text: About 80 °C is the self-heating selenium-stock temperature. The source separately describes CdSe precipitation at room temperature; no stock-cooling interval is given.

scopeLabel: Complete supplied four-page main, Figures 1–4, equations 1–5 and all 17 references. SI and cited full sources unreviewed. One actual quantified preparation, with two precursor mixtures and a separately described optical aliquot; no invented comparison batches. Independent source comparison passed; presentation pending.

bindings.caption: Add 0.56 mol NaOH and 0.0025 mol elemental Se to 50 mL distilled water. Their relative addition order is not specified. Dissolution of NaOH produces heat; the mixture reaches about 80 °C in a few minutes, allowing Se to dissolve. Geometry is original conceptual equipment, not measured source apparatus.

Add 0.0026 mol CdCl2·2.5H2O to 10 mL of 0.3 M aqueous EDTA solution. Starting EDTA salt and exact mixing duration are unreported. Geometry is original conceptual equipment, not measured source apparatus.

Combine the cadmium-complex mixture with the alkaline selenium solution through rapid stirring. The source reports room-temperature reaction under atmospheric pressure and immediate red-brown precipitation; it does not describe cooling/equilibration after the stock exotherm or give a numeric hold time. Geometry is original conceptual equipment, not measured source apparatus.
Filter the precipitate. Filtration hardware and duration are not described. Geometry is original conceptual equipment, not measured source apparatus.

Wash with dilute 0.1 M HCl solution and distilled water. Their exact sequence, amounts and repetition count are not specified. Geometry is original conceptual equipment, not measured source apparatus.

Dry the washed precipitate under vacuum at 50 °C for 4 h, then collect the final product for characterization. Vacuum pressure and yield are not reported. Geometry is original conceptual equipment, not measured source apparatus.

general_background.title: Formation from dissolved precursors
general_background.summary: When dissolved species become supersaturated with respect to a solid, nucleation and growth can compete with continued precursor conversion. Mixing, complexation and solution chemistry can change that balance.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Mechanisms of Nucleation and Growth of Nanoparticles in Solution

general_background.title: From a metal precursor to reactive species
general_background.summary: A metal precursor supplies the metal, while its ligands and conversion chemistry influence how reactive species become available. Stronger or more persistent coordination can slow release of reactive metal species, while ligand exchange can open alternative conversion pathways.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Mechanisms of Nucleation and Growth of Nanoparticles in Solution

general_background.title: Conversion of a nonmetal precursor
general_background.summary: Chalcogen and pnictogen precursors can differ in how they release or transfer the element during a reaction. Bonding, coordination and the reaction medium can influence the activation or transfer steps that make an element available for growth.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation
